text: Git branching is an important part of version control. A branch lets you work on new features without changing the main code. Developers often create feature branches to add new ideas safely. When the work is finished, they merge the branch back into the main project. Before merging, teams usually open a pull request so others can review the changes. This workflow keeps the code organized and reduces mistakes. If something goes wrong, you can easily switch back to another branch. Learning how branches, merging, and pull requests work together will make you a more confident developer.
